topics.title: Developer reference
topics.subtitle: How our SyteLine forms work under the hood, and how to build on them
topics.summary: For developers: how-to guides, the form events we use and what we learned about them, our IDO and UET fields, form components, scripting rules and the help link API.

blocks.text: Everything we have learned building **eCMRs**, **Service Orders** and **Incidents**, written down so the next form doesn't have to find it out again. Start with the how-to guides; the reference pages explain each piece.
Every change to a form goes in the form XML, built by the project's script and imported through **FormSync**. Design Mode is only for looking. See [Conventions](/syteline/dev/conventions).

topics.title: Add right-click Help to a form
topics.subtitle: Open the Enflite help page for the field the user is in
topics.summary: Handle StdFormHelp and StdFormComponentHelp in the form XML so Help opens the Enflite help page for the focused field. Confirmed on eCMRs.

blocks.text: Right-click a field → **Help** (and **F1**) normally opens Infor's help. This guide makes it open the Enflite help page for the field the user is in: the form works out the field, builds a `/go` link and opens it. The help site then picks the page.
Worked example: eCMRs (`tools/apply_form_changes.py`, `focus_help`). Confirmed on TRN 2026-09-30 (right-click → Help). Service Orders and Incidents use the same script.
Before you start

items: The form has a build script in `tools/` that writes the form XML. You add the handlers there, not in Design Mode.
The help site has pages for the form's fields, with the component names in their `aliases`. See [Add help pages for a form](/syteline/dev/guide-help-pages).
Pick a form variable name for the link: `EcmrsHelpUrl` on eCMRs, `ENF_HelpUrl` on Service Orders and Incidents.

blocks.text: 1. Add the variable
Add a form variable (e.g. `ENF_HelpUrl`) in the XML. The script writes the link into it; the next step reads it.
2. Handle both Help events
SyteLine raises **`StdFormHelp`** for right-click → **Help** (confirmed on TRN) and **`StdFormComponentHelp`** for **F1**. Give each two handlers:

head: Sequence
Response type
Response
rows: The script below: find the focused field, write the link into the variable

blocks.title: Step 0: the script (ResponseType 33)
blocks.text:
SCRIPTTEXT(Option Explicit On
Option Strict Off
Imports System
Imports Mongoose.Scripting
Namespace SyteLine.GlobalScripts
Public Class EvHandler_<Event>_0
Inherits GlobalScript
Sub Main()
Dim c As String = "", v As String = "focusempty", e As String = ""
Try
c = ThisForm.GetCurrentComponentName()
If c <> "" Then v = "focus"
Catch x As Exception
v = "focuserr"
e = x.Message
End Try
ThisForm.Variables("<HelpVar>").Value = "<HELP_SITE>/go/syteline/<form>" & If(c = "", "", "/" & c) & "?via=" & v & "&ev=<ev>&e=" & Uri.EscapeDataString(If(e.Length > 200, e.Substring(0, 200), e))
ReturnValue = "0"
End Sub
End Class
End Namespace
)

Replace `<HELP_SITE>` with `https://help-seven-xi.vercel.app`, `<form>` with the help site's form path (`ecmrs`, `service-orders`, `incidents`), `<HelpVar>` with your variable and `<ev>` with `form` (StdFormHelp) or `field` (StdFormComponentHelp).

No apostrophes anywhere in the script, not even in a comment: SyteLine reads `'` as a quote and reports *SCRIPTTEXT keyword required*. Scripts over 500 characters are split into `<Response>` and `<Response2>`; the whole script must stay under 1,500. The eCMRs build script checks both.
3. Build, import and test

items: Run the build script and its `--check`. The XML must keep its BOM and CRLF line endings.
Import the XML through **FormSync** at **Site** scope on TRN.
Open the form, **click into a field**, then right-click it → **Help**. The field's help page opens in a new tab.

blocks.text: Check it worked
The help site logs one line per click (Vercel → Logs):

blocks.title: Help site log
blocks.text: help link syteline/ecmrs component=c_item via=focus ev=form -> /syteline/ecmrs/fields/item

head: `via=`
Means
rows: The script found the focused field. Working.
No field had focus: the user right-clicked without clicking into a field first. The form's page opens.

blocks.text: Frequently asked questions

items: Why does the user have to click into the field first?
Help events don't say which component was right-clicked; the script can only ask which one has focus (`GetCurrentComponentName()`). Right-clicking doesn't move the focus.
Why not set `HelpFileName` on each field?
SyteLine always puts Infor's help address in front of it, so it can only open pages on Infor's help site (confirmed on TRN 2026-09-29).
Can the script read the event's parameters to find the field?

We tried (`CountParameter` / `GetParameter`, and the `ParameterCount` spelling): they didn't compile in the web client (*Error compiling script EvHandler_StdFormHelp_0*). Help events only carry parameters their handler defines, so they would not name the field anyway.
Can `StdFormComponentHelp` raise another event to share one script?
Don't: when it did (eCMRs#17) the right-click menu stopped opening. Each Help event runs its own copy of the script.
A **Your pop-up Blocker may be enabled** dialog appears
The page opens after the script, not straight from the click, so the browser treats it as a pop-up. Allow pop-ups for the SyteLine address (per user, or by IT policy `PopupsAllowedForUrls`).
What happens on Infor fields of a form we customize?
The help site sends them to Infor's own help. See [Send Infor fields to Infor's help](/syteline/dev/guide-infor-help).

topics.title: Add help pages for a form
topics.subtitle: One page per field, linked to its components
topics.summary: Add a form's field pages to content/, list each field's component names in aliases so right-click Help finds them, check and seed.

blocks.text: Right-click Help finds a field's page by the component name SyteLine sends. Each field page lists its components in `aliases`.
Worked example: `content/syteline/ecmrs.json` (a form page plus 55 field pages).
Before you start

items: Get the component names from the form XML: the field (`c_item`, `UfEvalDateEdit`), its label and its grid column.
Have the team's source for what each field means.

blocks.text: 1. Add the pages

items: In `content/syteline/<form>.json`, add the form page (path `<form>`, type `form`) with a `groups` list for its sections.
Add one page per field: path `<form>/fields/<name>`, type `field`, `parent` the form, `group` its section.
Put every component of the field in `aliases`: `["c_item", "l_item", "grid_item"]`.
Write the body: what it means, how to fill it in, values, good to know (see any eCMRs field page).

blocks.text: 2. Check and publish

items: Run `npm run check`. It fails if two pages claim the same component or a link points nowhere.
Commit, open a pull request, merge.
After the deploy, run `npm run seed` so the database has the new pages.

blocks.text: Check it worked
Open `https://help-seven-xi.vercel.app/go/syteline/<form>/<component>`: it should land on the field's page. That is exactly the link the form sends.
Frequently asked questions

items: Does letter case matter?
No: `/go` matches component names in any case.
What if a component has no page?
On our own forms, the form's page opens with a note naming the component. On an Infor form we customize, Infor's help opens.

topics.title: Send Infor fields to Infor's help
topics.subtitle: On forms we customize: our fields to our pages, Infor's to Infor's
topics.summary: Give the form page an infor block so Help on an Infor field opens Infor's field or form topic, while our UET fields open Enflite pages.

blocks.text: Service Orders and Incidents are Infor's forms with our UET fields added. Help on one of our fields opens our page; on any other field it should open Infor's help, as it did before.
Worked example: the `infor` block on `service-orders` and `incidents` ([Enflite/help#13](https://github.com/Enflite/help/pull/13)). Not confirmed on TRN yet.
Steps

items: Find Infor's topic for the form in its help library's `sitemap.html` (`https://docs.infor.com/csi/latest/en-us/csbiolh/`).
On the form page in `content/`, add `"infor": { "url": "<form topic>", "components": { "<Infor component>": "<field topic>" } }`. Only list components that have their own Infor topic.
`npm run check` (Infor addresses must be `https://`), merge, deploy, `npm run seed`.

blocks.text: How /go decides
The form XML doesn't change: fixing an Infor address never needs a SyteLine import.

topics.title: Fill in a value when a record is created
topics.subtitle: StdObjectNewCompleted: e.g. a record number on New
topics.summary: Use a StdObjectNewCompleted inline script to set a property (such as the key) when the user clicks New. Confirmed on eCMRs (CMR Num).

blocks.text: To fill a property the moment the user clicks **New** (a generated number, a default), handle **`StdObjectNewCompleted`**.
Worked example: eCMRs sets **CMR Num** to `CMR-YYMMDD-HHMMSS`. Confirmed on TRN 2026-09-29.
Steps

items: Add a `StdObjectNewCompleted` handler, sequence 0, ResponseType 33, with `COLID(object)` after the script.
In the script, only set the value if it is empty, then set it with `SetCurrentObjectPropertyPlusModifyRefresh` so the form shows it.
Build, import through FormSync, click **New**: the value appears.

blocks.title: StdObjectNewCompleted, sequence 0 (eCMRs)
blocks.text:
SCRIPTTEXT(Option Explicit On
Option Strict On

Imports System
Imports Microsoft.VisualBasic
Imports Mongoose.IDO.Protocol
Imports Mongoose.Scripting

Namespace SyteLine.GlobalScripts
Public Class EvHandler_StdObjectNewCompleted_0
Inherits GlobalScript

Sub Main()
            If ThisForm.PrimaryIDOCollection.CurrentItem.Properties.Item("CmrNum").GetValueOfString("") = "" Then
                ThisForm.PrimaryIDOCollection.SetCurrentObjectPropertyPlusModifyRefresh("CmrNum", "CMR-" & DateTime.Now.ToString("yyMMdd-HHmmss"))
            End If
End Sub
End Class
End Namespace
) COLID(object)
Frequently asked questions

items: Why not the IDO's Default Value?
It only takes keywords like `AUTONUMBER(...)`, can't add a prefix, and on eCMRs AUTONUMBER repeated numbers (save failed on `PK_ue_ecmrs`).
Two records created in the same second?
They get the same number and the second save fails; save again.

topics.title: Fill a description from a drop-down
topics.subtitle: DefaultFrom or SetPropertyFromList, never SelectionEvent
topics.summary: When the user picks a code, fill its description into another field: DefaultFrom for Item and Vendor, the SetPropertyFromList validator for Dept and Work Center.

blocks.text: Picking an Item, Vendor, Dept or Work Center should fill its description. There are two mechanisms that work, and one that breaks the whole form.
Never use a `SelectionEvent` (ResponseType 49 with `FILTER()/MOV()/SONON()/SETP()`) on a drop-down: after one use the whole form locks, with no error. Confirmed on eCMRs.
Option A: DefaultFrom

On the code field's component: `<DefaultFrom>Item(ItemDescription)</DefaultFrom>`, with `PropertyClassName` `Item`. Confirmed on eCMRs for `Item(ItemDescription)`, `Item(NextAssyDescription)` and `VendNum(VendorName)`.
Don't use it with a system class that carries an address, such as `Dept`: it failed with *Bad SETPROPERTIES specification in validator Dept: this cache property OfcAddr4 not in cache*.
Option B: SetPropertyFromList

items: Give the code field a list that includes the description: `SLDepts( PROPERTIES(Dept, Description) )`.
Add the validator `SetPropertyFromList(DeptDescription, Description)`: copy the list's `Description` column into `DeptDescription`.
Turn on **Validate Immediately** (bit 32 of the component's `<Flags>`, e.g. `33`), or the description only fills on save.

blocks.text: Confirmed on eCMRs 2026-09-29 (Dept `100` → **Operations**, Work Center `BRAZE` → **Brazing**). Validate Immediately: not confirmed yet.
For both

items: The description property must have **Read Only Record** cleared on the IDO, or the form locks after the pick.
The description field's component stays a bare edit box: no list source of its own (a leftover `ComboListSource` locked the form).

topics.title: Add a fixed drop-down list
topics.subtitle: An Inline List on the IDO property
topics.summary: Put a fixed list of values (Priority, Status) on the IDO property as an Inline List, then Check In the IDO.

blocks.text: For a drop-down with a fixed list of values, the list lives on the **IDO property**, not in the form.
Worked example: eCMRs Status, Priority, Initial Change, Dispositions, Reason and Cause Code. Confirmed on TRN.
Steps

items: In **IDO Properties**, open the property. Leave **Property Class** blank.
In **Inline List**, enter `ENTRIES(High,Medium,Low)`.
**Check In** the IDO. Until you do, saving the form fails with *Missing property data type for ue_ecmrs.<Property>*.
The form's component needs no list source of its own: it picks the list up from the property.

blocks.text: Frequently asked questions

items: Can I use an Infor list instead (a PropertyClassName like QCReasonCode)?
Only if its filters work on your IDO: QCReasonCode's list filters on QC_MRRs fields with `FP(...)`, and on eCMRs it failed with *'FP' is not a recognized built-in function name*.
Can FormSync or a CSV import set the Inline List?
The IDO Properties import can; FormSync can't. Always check it in Application Studio after an import.

topics.title: Add a UET field to an Infor form
topics.subtitle: New fields on Infor's table, without changing Infor's objects
topics.summary: Create the UET user field, class and relationships, run Impact Schema, check the runtime property, then bind the form to <alias>Uf_ENF_<Name>.

blocks.text: To add fields to one of Infor's forms (Service Orders, Incidents), extend Infor's table with **UET**. Infor's IDO picks the fields up by itself; you never edit it.
Worked example: Service Orders (`Enflite/ServiceOrders`, `docs/Implementation-Plan.md`) and Incidents.
Before you start

items: Back up the form with FormSync ([Back up a form](/syteline/build/back-up-a-form)).
Name the fields `Uf_ENF_<Name>` and the class `ENF_<Area>`.

blocks.text: 1. UET setup, in this order

items: **User Defined Types** (for fixed values, e.g. `ENF_ZeroTime`: Yes, No).
**UET User Fields**. Dates: User Data Type `Date4Type`, Data Type `datetime` (re-open the field to check; `nvarchar` shows dates as `20260909 00:00:00.000`).
**UET Classes**.
**UET Class/Field Relationships**.
**UET Table/Class Relationships**: the `_mst` table (e.g. `fs_sro_mst`), **Active** ✔, **Extend All Records** ✔.

blocks.text: 2. Impact Schema

items: Get users out of the form.
Tick **Commit Form Changes** and **Impact Schema**, then **Process**.
When the background task finishes with no errors, run **Unload IDO Metadata**, and sign out and back in.

blocks.text: 3. Check the property exists

Open the current form in Design Mode, select any edit box and open its **Data Source** list (cancel without saving). The field is listed as `<alias>Uf_ENF_<Name>`: `sroUf_ENF_EvalDate` on Service Orders.
These runtime properties don't appear in the IDOs → Properties export, so don't use that to check. Never bind to the `Der<alias>ExtBy…` helper properties.
4. Bind the form

items: In the build script, bind the new component to `object.<alias>Uf_ENF_<Name>` (pass the alias as `--prefix`).
Highlight new components in purple, add a grid column, rebuild, import through FormSync at Site scope.
Fill each field, save, reopen: no *Invalid property name*, values kept.

topics.title: Form events and event handlers
topics.subtitle: How a form reacts to what the user does
topics.summary: How SyteLine event handlers work (name, sequence, response type), the response types we use, and every event on our forms.

blocks.text: A form reacts through **event handlers**. SyteLine raises an event (the user clicks **New**, asks for **Help**, a button generates one); every handler with that event name runs, in **Sequence** order. Each handler has a **Response Type** that says what its **Response** is.

blocks.title: An event handler in the form XML
blocks.text:
<EventHandler Name="StdFormHelp" Sequence="1">
   <ResponseType>39</ResponseType>
   <Response>URL(V(EcmrsHelpUrl)) ( )</Response>
</EventHandler>

What it does

blocks.text: What we learned

items: `EventToGenerate` fires custom events from **buttons** and **check boxes**. On a drop-down it fired, did nothing and gave no error.
`SelectionEvent` on a drop-down locks the whole form after one use. Don't use it.
FormSync keeps a handler's setting that is missing from the file. To remove a setting, give the event or component a new name so FormSync creates it fresh.
A handler that raises another event from inside `StdFormComponentHelp` stopped the right-click menu opening (eCMRs#17).

topics.title: Inline scripts (ResponseType 33)
topics.subtitle: The rules the web client enforces
topics.summary: How inline VB scripts are stored and what SyteLine's web client accepts: SCRIPTTEXT, no apostrophes, 500/1500 characters, no late binding, ThisForm calls that work.

blocks.text: An inline script is VB.NET inside `SCRIPTTEXT( ... )`, compiled by SyteLine when the event first runs. Copy the class wrapper from a working script and change only `Sub Main()`.

blocks.title: Skeleton
blocks.text:
SCRIPTTEXT(Option Explicit On
Option Strict Off
Imports System
Imports Mongoose.Scripting
Namespace SyteLine.GlobalScripts
Public Class EvHandler_<Event>_<Sequence>
Inherits GlobalScript
Sub Main()
  ...
  ReturnValue = "0"
End Sub
End Class
End Namespace
)
Rules

head: Rule
Otherwise
rows: No apostrophes, including VB comments (`' ...`) and words like `server's`
*SCRIPTTEXT keyword required for InlineScript event handlers*
Store over 500 characters as `<Response>` (500) + `<Response2>`, as Infor's exports do
Keep the whole script under 1,500 characters
Call `ThisForm.…` directly, never through `Dim f As Object = ThisForm`
*Attempt by method ...InvokeMethod... to access method ...ScriptForm.Variables failed*
Later handler steps may not run

blocks.text: Calls we know work in the web client
Calls that don't

head: Call
Result
rows: Doesn't compile. Use `USERNAME()` in a ResponseType 22 step

blocks.text: When a script fails silently, have it put the error text somewhere you can see (the eCMRs Help script sends it to the help site as `&e=`).

topics.title: Form components: lists, auto-fill and flags
topics.subtitle: The component settings we use in the form XML
topics.summary: Drop-down lists (ComboListSource, DISPLAY order), DefaultFrom, validators, Validate Immediately, Caption, Read Only Record, and why FormSync keeps old settings.

head: Setting
Syntax
What we learned
rows: The drop-down stores the **first column in `DISPLAY()`**. With `DISPLAY(2,1,3)` PO Line stored the Item and saves failed (*Data length for ... is greater than effective length*).
`P(x)` is the current value of property x. `FP(x)` is an exact match: no wildcard, no padding.
Fills another property from the picked value's class. Works for Item and VendNum; broke with Dept. See [Fill a description](/syteline/dev/guide-description-autofill).
Copies one list column into one property. Named system validators (`Dept`, `WcDesc`) write properties our IDO doesn't have.
Without it, validators run only on save.
Links the field to its label, so messages name the right field.
Brings the class's list and validators with it. Infor's QC classes filter on QC_MRRs fields and failed on eCMRs.
Fires custom events from buttons and check boxes; not from drop-downs.

blocks.text: Settings on the IDO, not the form

head: Setting
What we learned
rows: A field the form writes to (a description, a name filled from a list) must have it cleared, or the whole form locks after the first edit, silently. FormSync and CSV imports don't change it on an existing property: clear it in Application Studio.
`ENTRIES(a,b,c)` on the property; then **Check In**. See [Add a fixed drop-down list](/syteline/dev/guide-fixed-list).

blocks.text: FormSync keeps settings missing from the file

Removing a line from the XML (say a `PropertyClassName`) and re-importing leaves the old setting in place. To drop it, give the component a new name (`c_reason_code_v2`) so FormSync creates it fresh, then remove the old one.

If the whole form greys out after one edit with no error, check first: the target property's **Read Only Record** on the IDO, then a `SelectionEvent`, then a leftover list source on the target component.

topics.title: Conventions
topics.subtitle: Naming, files and delivery rules for every Enflite form repo
topics.summary: Enflite naming (ENF, Uf_ENF_, ue_), how form XML is built and delivered, and the rules every form repo follows.

blocks.text: The full standard is `AGENTS.md` in every form repo (master copy in `Enflite/Form-Project-Templates`).

blocks.text: Delivery rules

items: TRN first, then production, from the same files.
Never change Infor's tables, IDOs or Vendor forms.
Every change goes in the build script, which writes the form XML. Never hand-edit the XML, never deliver from Design Mode.
Form XML keeps its UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line endings (`.gitattributes`: `*.xml -text`). Scripts edit the text in place; never re-serialize it with an XML parser.
Back up (export) the form from each environment before its first import, into `original/`.
Import through **FormSync** at **Site** scope.
New and changed components are highlighted purple until the team signs off.

topics.title: UET fields: Service Orders and Incidents
topics.subtitle: Our fields on Infor's tables, and how the forms reach them
topics.summary: The UET classes, user fields and runtime property names on Service Orders (fs_sro_mst) and Incidents (fs_incident_mst).

blocks.text: Service Orders: IDO `FSP.FSSROs`, table `fs_sro` (alias `sro`).
Incidents: IDO `FSIncidents`, table `fs_incident`.
Not confirmed: the Incidents alias `inc` is assumed until Staging check A on TRN lists `incUf_ENF_DateOfManufacture`.
How the form reaches a UET field

items: After Impact Schema and **Unload IDO Metadata**, the IDO has a runtime property `<alias>Uf_ENF_<Name>` for each field. Nothing is added to the IDO by hand.
The runtime properties don't appear in the IDO Properties export. Check in Design Mode's Data Source list or a throw-away Dataview.
CyberQuery reads the same `sroUf_ENF_…` properties from `FSSROs`.
